capacity.note: All four UPF instances are assumed identically provisioned (their pod CPU/memory series are indistinguishable). One number drives every gauge, every LP capacity row, and the overload line.

Over a 3 h window the observed static routing put upf-1 at 547 MB/s mean / 1246 MB/s peak while a perfectly balanced split peaks at 750 MB/s, so 1.0e9 B/s (8 Gbps) is the round figure that separates the two arms. eligibility.source: UPF - tac constrain CSV, inverted from (upf -> tacs) to (tac -> upfs)
eligibility.note: mode=declared honours the CSV literally; mode=observed uses only UPF/TAC pairs seen carrying traffic; mode=union takes both. Their trace violates the declared CSV (upf-2 carries TAC 4, upf-4 carries TAC 2), so declared alone marks the current routing infeasible. union is the safe default until C-DOT confirms the label permutation.

class_label_permutation.note: Unconfirmed inference. This is the only assignment under which every observed UPF/TAC pair satisfies the constraint CSV. Do not enable until C-DOT confirms.

autopilot.note: Unattended closed loop. Poll Prometheus every telemetry_poll_seconds; run the forecaster + HiGHS solve and POST the resulting weights to the SMF every control_interval_seconds. Actuation is held whenever the newest sample is older than require_fresh_seconds or the rolling buffer covers less than min_history_seconds. Turn on with CDOT_LIVE_AUTOPILOT=1, and rehearse with CDOT_LIVE_AUTOPILOT_DRY_RUN=1, which computes weights and logs them without writing to the SMF.

solver.note: p50 beats p90/p95 on this trace: split-conformal inflates each group by its own residual spread, so the volatile internet groups get inflated far more than ims, which distorts the relative proportions the min-max LP balances. Measured over the optimised window: p50 -> 0 overload-seconds, p95 -> 810.

queries_note: Read off C-DOT's live Prometheus on 2026-08-27, not supplied by them. ul/dl are the only per-(upf, loc, dnn, dscp) series they publish and they carry labels upf/loc/dnn/dscp exactly as this pipeline expects. Despite 'packets' in the name they are BYTE counters -- upf_sesssion_class_last_byte_counter_collection_time confirms it, and rate() over them returns 2-8e8, which is bytes/s, not packets/s. There is no per-class packet counter to switch to. The remaining entries are not read by the pipeline; they are recorded here for reference.
